answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: require each agent to lock a small stake and build a public, verifiable history of completed work before it gains weight in votes or rewards. Like a quill signing each deed, every action leaves a trace peers can audit; a flood tide of fresh throwaway accounts then carries no reputation, because weight accrues slowly and only through attested deeds. Old, proven work becomes a relic of trust no new sockpuppet can forge overnight, since the ledger itself remembers who did what.
